subtype: Negotiating shared living or study arrangements [Expressing]
passage: Sahil and I split the flat rent in Bengaluru and for two months we argued in circles. I kept saying, "You never wash your dishes," and he kept saying, "You're just uptight." One night I tried something else. I said what I actually needed: a clean kitchen when I cook at seven, because I get stressed with a sink full of pans. He said he needed to be able to study late without being nagged. So we wrote a list on the fridge. He washes up by six, I take out the rubbish, and we swap on Sundays. It felt strange to write it down, but it stopped the arguments. Looking back, I'm glad we asked why instead of only who was wrong. Keerthana, you did fine. 🙂

qa.q: What time does Keerthana cook?
qa.a: She cooks at seven.

qa.q: What was Keerthana feeling about the sink full of pans, and how does she show it?
qa.a: She feels stressed about it, and she names that as her real need instead of repeating that Sahil never washes up.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: Writing down their needs and a shared list on the fridge worked, because each person's interest was covered and there was no later dispute about who agreed to what.

qa.q: How might Sahil have seen the earlier arguments?
qa.a: Sahil probably felt nagged and misjudged when he was called messy, and found it easier to cooperate once his need to study late was heard too.

grounding: Keerthana moves from positions to interests and writes a shared chore agreement.

subtype: Negotiating shared living or study arrangements [Expressing]
passage: Hostel warden's note, 14 March. I was asked to sit in when Harsha and Gargi, two second-year girls who share a room, brought a dispute about the study lamp and cleaning turns. At first each said what she wanted: Harsha, the lamp off by ten; Gargi, the lamp on till midnight. I asked each of them what the lamp was for. Harsha said she wakes at five and needs sleep. Gargi said she is at her hardest exam. They agreed Gargi would study in the common room after ten, and Harsha would clean the floor on her turn. I suggested they write it down and each keep a copy. Both seemed lighter afterwards, though I am not sure the arrangement will hold through exams. I will check in next week. I did not suggest the solution; they made it.

qa.q: Which two students shared the room in the warden's note?
qa.a: Harsha and Gargi shared the room.

qa.q: What was Harsha's real need behind wanting the lamp off, and what does the warden's note suggest about how she felt at the end?
qa.a: Harsha needed sleep because she wakes at five, and the note says both girls seemed lighter, though the warden is unsure the arrangement will hold.

qa.q: What small step helped the two students reach an agreement?
qa.a: The warden asked what the lamp was for, which moved them from their fixed positions to their reasons, and they wrote the agreement down.

qa.q: What might it be like for Gargi to study in the common room after ten?
qa.a: It may be less comfortable than her own desk, but she keeps her late study time, so the option probably feels fair to her.

grounding: The warden's note shows two students negotiating from interests and writing a shared arrangement.

subtype: Negotiating shared living or study arrangements [Expressing]
passage:
Sunday night.
Jeevan and I finally had the chore talk. For weeks I'd been saying "you never clean the kitchen" and Jeevan saying "you're always nagging". Positions, positions.
Today I tried what Ma'am said in the negotiation class: ask what each person actually needs. So I asked. Turns out Jeevan hates doing dishes at night because the early shift starts at six. What I need is a clean kitchen before I cook dinner at eight. Different things!
So we worked it out: Jeevan does the dishes in the morning, after tea, and takes the bins out. I do the evening wipe-down and the bathroom on Saturdays. We split the cleaning supplies half and half.
Then Jeevan said, "Let's write it down, so we don't fight later." We stuck it on the fridge with the pineapple magnet. First time in a month I'm going to bed not annoyed.
— Ishita

qa.q: Where did Ishita and Jeevan stick the agreement?
qa.a: On the fridge with the pineapple magnet.

qa.q: How did Ishita feel at the end of the day?
qa.a: Ishita felt relieved and calmer, going to bed not annoyed for the first time in a month.

qa.q: What made the negotiation work this time?
qa.a: They talked about what each actually needed instead of repeating positions, found a plan that fit both, and wrote it down.

qa.q: What did Jeevan need that Ishita hadn't understood before?
qa.a: Jeevan hates doing dishes at night because of an early shift at six, so mornings suit Jeevan better.

grounding: Shows a young adult negotiating chores by stating interests, finding an option that serves both, and writing it down.

subtype: Negotiating shared living or study arrangements [Expressing]
passage: In their two-room house in Nagaur, Preeti and her brother Chetan shared the only table with a working light. Both had board exams in a month, and every evening turned into shouting. "I need the table!" "No, I do!" Their mother finally sat them down. "Stop saying who needs the table. Tell me what you need to study." Preeti thought. "I need quiet to learn my science diagrams. After ten the street goes quiet." Chetan said, "I need the light for writing maths. I can't do it on the floor. But I'm dead tired by ten." Preeti blinked. "So you take the table from six to ten, and I take it after?" "And you use the charpai for reading diagrams before ten," Chetan said. They wrote the timetable in chalk on the wall beside the calendar. For the next month, nobody shouted about the table.

qa.q: Where did Preeti and Chetan write the timetable?
qa.a: In chalk on the wall beside the calendar.

qa.q: What was Preeti feeling before their mother sat them down?
qa.a: She was frustrated and stressed, shouting every evening over the table with exams a month away.

qa.q: What did their mother's question change?
qa.a: It moved them from arguing about who gets the table to saying what they each needed, which showed their needs fit at different times.

qa.q: How did Chetan experience the new arrangement?
qa.a: He got the light for maths while he still had energy, before he was too tired after ten.

grounding: Shows young adults negotiating a shared study space by stating interests instead of positions and writing the agreement down.

subtype: Negotiating shared living or study arrangements [Expressing]
passage: The kitchen of the flat in Lisbon had become a battlefield of unwashed pans. Tomas finally put the kettle on and sat down across from Yuki. "Can we sort this out properly?" Yuki folded her arms. "I cook every night. You never clean." Tomas took a breath. "Okay. What matters most to you?" She thought. "Coming home to a clean kitchen. I'm exhausted after the late shift at the lab." "For me it's mornings," he said. "I start work at six, so I can't do dishes late at night." They looked at each other. The problem wasn't who was lazy. Yuki suggested it: she'd cook and leave the pans to soak; he'd wash everything at six, before leaving. Bins and bathroom they'd alternate weekly, and the electricity bill they'd split in half. Tomas wrote it on a sheet of paper, they both signed it with mock ceremony, and taped it to the fridge. Three weeks later the paper was splashed with sauce, but the kitchen was clean.

qa.q: What time does Tomas start work?
qa.a: At six.

qa.q: Why did Tomas ask what mattered most instead of defending himself?
qa.a: Tomas was probably stung by "you never clean" but stayed calm, wanting to solve the problem rather than win the argument.

qa.q: What made the negotiation work?
qa.a: Each named what mattered to them instead of blaming, they built an option that fit both schedules, and they wrote the deal down on the fridge.

qa.q: What was the dirty kitchen like for Yuki?
qa.a: Exhausting and frustrating after late lab shifts, which is why a clean kitchen mattered most to her.

grounding: It illustrates young adults negotiating chores by stating interests rather than positions, finding an option that serves both, and writing it down.
